content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer | Java, Spring Boot, APIs & Event-Driven Systems

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with professional experience designing, building and operating Java backend services for insurance and travel products. Experienced with REST APIs, relational databases, Kafka-based event integration, automated testing, CI/CD and AWS-based Kubernetes deployments. Focused on service reliability, API performance and production quality.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java (8–17), Kotlin (basic)
Backend & APIs: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, REST, OpenAPI
Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ
Databases & caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis
Cloud & delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins
Testing & tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Lisbon
Jan 2022–Present
- Develop and maintain seven Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned the REST API for partner quoting integration, documented with OpenAPI and used by 12 broker partners.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for claims workflows; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table to eliminate duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote-endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes (EKS) using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in the on-call rota one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A. | Porto
Sep 2019–Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Contributed to breaking up the monolith by extracting a notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-Time) | CodeFarol Lda | Porto
Jul 2018–Aug 2019
- Performed PHP and later Java maintenance work for small-business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018

LANGUAGES
English (fluent) | Portuguese (fluent) | Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, and professional CV with a clear backend-engineering focus. The experience section uses measurable outcomes effectively, including seven microservices, 12 broker partners, latency reduction from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, and test-coverage improvement from 35% to 70%. The bullets demonstrate production ownership, API design, event-driven systems, performance work, testing, deployment, and on-call responsibility. Education, languages, contact details, and technical skills are complete and easy to locate. The main content limitation is that it does not provide direct evidence of explaining technical trade-offs or writing design documentation, and it does not establish willingness to work mainly in Python; these are alignment limitations rather than clear writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard headings, simple text structure, conventional job titles, searchable technology names, and reverse-chronological experience. It contains strong matches for Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, AWS, Kubernetes, automated testing, and CI/CD. AI screening probability is high for the comparable-language backend requirement and most technical must-haves. Minor keyword opportunities remain: the document demonstrates query tuning through the JPA N+1 fix but does not use the exact phrase "query tuning"; Jenkins pipelines support CI/CD but the skills section does not explicitly say "CI/CD." Do not add Python, FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Terraform, observability tools, logistics, or schema migrations because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for the comparable-language pathway: the original information establishes seven years of Java/Spring Boot backend experience, and the CV clearly shows REST API design, Kafka event processing, PostgreSQL and other relational databases, query-performance work, Docker, AWS/EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, Jenkins pipelines, and fluent English. The event-driven and reliability experience is particularly relevant to Tessel's shipment-tracking platform and on-call culture. The principal alignment gap is Python: the candidate has no documented Python or FastAPI experience, and the provided material does not state willingness to work mainly in Python. Schema migrations are also not documented. Nice-to-have gaps include logistics or supply-chain experience, EDI formats, Terraform, observability tooling, and Dutch or French. The CV does show Kafka and Kubernetes, which are relevant nice-to-haves. These are candidate-profile gaps or unverified requirements, not defects that can be fixed by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the opening sentence from "Backend engineer with professional experience designing and building Java backend services" to "Backend engineer with 7 years of experience designing, building, and operating Java/Spring Boot backend services for insurance and travel products." This surfaces the exact experience duration from the original candidate information and strengthens the comparable-language match.
2. In the Technical Skills section under "Databases & caching," change the line to "Databases & caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis; query tuning and JPA performance optimization." This uses the job description's exact "query tuning" terminology while remaining supported by the documented Redis improvement and JPA N+1 remediation.
3. In the Technical Skills section under "Cloud & delivery," change "AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins" to "AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins, CI/CD pipelines." This makes the CI/CD capability explicit, supported by the Jenkins pipeline experience already documented.
4. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, revise the latency bullet from "Reduced quote-endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries" to "Reduced quote-endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through query tuning, Redis caching, and resolution of JPA N+1 queries." This preserves the factual result while improving keyword alignment for performance and query-tuning screening.
